title: Power Automate: schedule desktop flows directly with scheduled triggers
summary: Hold: the briefing says recurring desktop flows require a scheduled cloud flow, although Microsoft documents another route and the launched roadmap feature removes that requirement. It also overstates the absence of licensing information and the inevitability of charges, and its data-policy instructions stop short of configuring the stated control.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Recurring runs increase the run count used for usage-based charging.
claims.quote: The Power Automate meters enable users to build and/or run premium Power Automate flows and to pay for their usage based on the number of times these flows run instead of purchasing standalone Power Automate licenses.

claims.claim: Every recurring run adds spend in a pay-as-you-go environment.
claims.quote: Attended runs follow the entitlements of the user running the flow. A user whose license includes attended RPA isn't charged; a user whose license doesn't include it is charged $0.60 per run.
claims.fix: Replace 'every recurring run adds to run counts, machine queues and, in pay-as-you-go environments, spend' with 'recurring runs increase run counts and machine demand, and can increase pay-as-you-go charges depending on run mode and licence entitlements'. Keep the existing detailed rates and exemptions in Cost and licensing.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: data policy row
claims.claim: Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy reaches the control deciding which desktop modules and connectors can be used.
claims.quote: From the list of data policies, select a policy, and then select Edit Policy.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Move to Business'. The current path reaches the policy list, not classification. Qualify the note: 'To show desktop flow action groups in the UI, first enable Show desktop flow actions in DLP policies; modules must be explicitly classified.' That prerequisite is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-automate/prevent-data-loss.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: data policy row
claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy is the operation that configures which desktop modules and connectors may be used.
claims.quote: The New-DlpPolicy cmdlet creates a new DLP policy for the logged in admin's tenant.
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Connectors <connector-objects> -Classification <classification>' and set its docs URL to https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powerapps.administration.powershell/add-connectorstopolicy. State in the note: 'Classification accepts General, Confidential or Blocked for Non-business, Business or Blocked; connector objects contain id, type and name.' That reference explicitly includes desktop-flow modules. The current reference documents policy creation, not the classification operation the row promises.

claims.claim: A data policy can govern both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors within its environment scope.
claims.quote: You can define a DLP policy that manages both desktop flow modules and cloud flow connectors.

claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate "scheduled triggers" "data" policy identity connection; opened prevent-data-loss and automation-center-overview. General desktop-flow and connector governance is documented, but no direct-schedule-to-connector relationship is stated.
